reading.source: The Economist (public reprint via Hindustan Times)
reading.summaryKo: '세계의 백오피스'였던 인도 벵갈루루가 이제 우주·국방·반도체 같은 '딥테크' 도시로 변신 중이래요. 위성 스타트업 Pixxel(창업자 Awais Ahmed, 20살에 창업해 2억 달러 유치), 인도 첫 우주 유니콘 Skyroot 같은 회사가 대표적이고, 우주 스타트업이 10년 만에 1곳에서 400곳 이상이 됐어요. 1차 IT 붐은 정부와 상관없이 일어났지만, 이번엔 모디 정부의 규제 완화·조달·자금 지원이 큰 역할을 해요. 다만 부처 간 조율 부족, 성장 자금 부족, 안보 우려, 그리고 엉망인 도시 인프라(교통체증, 움푹 팬 도로)가 위험 요소래요.
excerpt: For decades Bangalore has powered India’s software and IT industry, as the home to giants that include Infosys, Wipro and TCS. Now the buzz in India’s startup capital is “deep tech”—a somewhat loosely applied term for products supposedly based on scientific breakthroughs or advanced engineering in sectors like space, defence and semiconductors.

India’s first tech boom happened largely in spite of the government. This time is different. India’s notoriously bureaucratic government has become highly involved in what it considers to be strategic sectors. When it loosens its grip, things take off.
reading.tip: 'in spite of'(~에도 불구하고)와 'This time is different'의 대비가 기사 전체 구조예요. 'not all plain sailing'(순탄치만은 않다), 'loosens its grip'(통제를 느슨하게 하다), 'take off'(급성장하다)도 Economist가 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.

writing.prompt: Write 3–5 sentences in English: Cramer says risk and return go hand in hand. Describe one time the market (or your own portfolio) fell sharply. How did you react?
writing.question: Next time stocks crash, what is your game plan?
writing.hint: 이런 표현을 써 보세요: When the market fell in ..., I ... / Looking back, I should have ... / Next time, my game plan is to ...

speaking.prompt: In one minute: Bangalore wants to become a deep-tech hub. Which Korean city or company do you think is strongest in deep tech (chips, bio, space)? Why?
phrases: I think ... is the strongest because ...
speaking.alt: 쉬운 버전: Say three short sentences (e.g. Korea is strong in chips. Samsung is a big company. I am proud of it.).

evening.note: 수요일, 한 주의 중간이에요. 지난번 읽은 데서 이어서 10페이지. 피곤하면 5페이지만, 아니면 Minimum day도 OK.

stuck.note: 샘플: 어제 막힌 문장 2개 · 문장당 2–3분 (이렇게 보여요)

items.from: Jim Cramer · CNBC · Mad Money · 11/25 듣기
items.text: Because portfolio managers could go in easily and out easily, though, the futures became the most powerful drivers of stock prices, particularly for hedge funds, even more powerful than the actual forms of the underlying companies that stocks are meant to represent.
items.why: 주어(the futures)가 앞의 Because절과 though 뒤에 숨어 있어요. 'Because ~, though,' = '그런데 ~했기 때문에'. 대본의 'forms'는 실제로는 firms(기업)로 말한 거예요.
chunks: that stocks are meant to represent.
items.paraphrase: Fund managers could buy and sell futures quickly, so futures moved stock prices more than the real companies behind the stocks did.
items.ko: 펀드매니저들이 선물은 쉽게 사고팔 수 있었기 때문에, 선물이 주가를 움직이는 가장 큰 힘이 됐어요. 주식이 원래 대표하는 실제 기업들보다도 더 강하게요.

items.text: Now the buzz in India’s startup capital is “deep tech”—a somewhat loosely applied term for products supposedly based on scientific breakthroughs or advanced engineering in sectors like space, defence and semiconductors.
items.why: 대시(—) 뒤는 'deep tech'를 풀어 설명하는 부분이에요. buzz = 화제·유행어, loosely applied = 대충(느슨하게) 붙이는, supposedly = ~라고들 하는(의심 섞임).
chunks: in sectors like space, defence and semiconductors.
items.paraphrase: Today everyone in Bangalore is talking about “deep tech”, a vague label for products said to come from real science or advanced engineering, in areas like space, defence and chips.
items.ko: 요즘 인도 스타트업 수도(벵갈루루)의 화두는 '딥테크'예요. 우주·국방·반도체처럼 과학적 돌파나 첨단 공학에 기반한다고들 하는 제품에 꽤 느슨하게 붙이는 말이죠.
